content.clinicalSnapshot: ⟦NAME_OF_PATIENT_RISK⟧ presents with a two-month recurrent depressive episode of severe intensity, marked by persistent low mood, anhedonia, early waking, poor appetite and pronounced fatigue. Functional decline is substantial: the patient has been absent from work for the past three weeks. Passive suicidal ideation is present several times a week, though without plan or intent. Regular evening alcohol use alongside current antidepressant treatment is a concurrent management consideration. A prior self-harm episode four years ago, now in the context of active passive ideation, warrants close monitoring.

diagnoses.name: Major Depressive Disorder, Recurrent Episode
diagnoses.rationale: This diagnosis accounts for the persistent low mood, anhedonia, early waking, poor appetite and marked fatigue over the past two months. The episode has produced substantial functional impairment, with three weeks of work absence.

Protective factors include the patient's spouse and weekly faith community, both identified as reasons for living.

risks.note: The patient reports taking sertraline 100 mg once daily and drinking alcohol on most evenings, approximately three drinks each time. Regular alcohol use alongside an SSRI antidepressant is a clinically relevant co-occurrence that may affect treatment response and carries additive central nervous system depressant risk. Confirm current alcohol intake, discuss the interaction, and assess whether a formal alcohol-use evaluation is warranted.

content.limitations: These findings are based on a structured self-report interview completed on a single occasion and reflect the patient's presentation at the time of assessment. Suicide risk is dynamic and can change rapidly; this letter does not predict future behaviour. Occupation, psychotherapy history and hospitalisation history were not captured in the case materials. Regular alcohol consumption was reported but a formal alcohol-use disorder screen was not administered.
